title: MSCA DN RESILIOUS awarded (€4.53M)
text: Our project RESILIOUS has been awarded €4.53M through the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Networks programme. The project will train 15 doctoral researchers and study Internet resilience across terrestrial, satellite and submarine infrastructure, including security, recovery, governance and standardisation; I am PI at QMUL.

title: IGF 2026 workshop selected
html: Our workshop ‘Can AI Change Who Shapes Open Internet Standards?’ has been selected for the Internet Governance Forum 2026. Co-organised with Dirk Kutscher, IRTF Chair, the session brings together Anriette Esterhuysen (Association for Progressive Communications), Adiel Akplogan (VP, Technical Engagement, ICANN), Mark Nottingham (Cloudflare), and Esteve Sanz (Head of Sector, Internet Governance and Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue, European Commission).

title: FediGuard accepted at ACM SIGMETRICS 2027
text: Our paper ‘FediGuard: Decentralized Content Moderation for the Fediverse’, by Jiahui He, Haris Bin Zia, Ignacio Castro, Peixian Zhang, Yupeng He and Gareth Tyson, has been accepted at ACM SIGMETRICS 2027. The work examines decentralised content moderation in the Fediverse and proposes FediGuard to support moderation across independently operated servers.

title: Dagstuhl Seminar on Internet resilience
text: I am co-organising Dagstuhl Seminar 27201, ‘Rethinking Internet Resilience in a Post-Global Era’, with Theophilus A. Benson, Jane R. Coffin and Dirk Kutscher. The seminar brings together researchers, operators, industry practitioners, economists and policy experts to examine Internet resilience by looking at its infrastructure and its concentration, as well as its governance.

title: Neighbourhood Signals awarded REPHRAIN Safer Streets funding
html: Our project ‘Neighbourhood Signals: Online Discussions and Crime’, with Waleed Iqbal, was awarded £23,794 through the REPHRAIN Safer Streets programme. The project investigates whether hyperlocal online discussions can provide signals of subsequent offline crime by linking longitudinal Nextdoor data with police-recorded crime and socio-demographic data.

title: Neighbourhood Signals at Eurocrim 2026
text: I was invited to Eurocrim 2026 in Warsaw to discuss our work on the relationship between hyperlocal online discussions and offline crime. I presented ‘Neighbourhood Signals: Investigating Hyperlocal Online Discussions as Indicators of Police-recorded Crime’ as part of the panel ‘Reconceptualising Crime in a Hybrid World: The Blurry Intersection between Online and Offline Harms’, and also took part in a roundtable discussing the broader implications of the findings.
